question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{0-6}{2-(-6)} \\  & =-\frac{6}{8} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{3}{4}$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-\frac{3}{4}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =-\frac{3}{4}x+b \\ 0 & =-\frac{3}{4}(2)+b \\ 0 & =-\frac{3}{2}+b \\ 0+\frac{3}{2} & =b \\ \frac{3}{2} & =b\end{aligned}
$$

So the equation of the line is $y=-\frac{3}{4}\,x+\frac{3}{2}.$
